column4: Visit note | 2026-05-16 10:30 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Fahim Pramanik, 70, male. Mr. Pramanik attends for a review regarding ongoing weakness and vomiting. He mentions that his symptoms started after drinking tap water on a trip to Lalbagh. He works as a homemaker and has a medical background of Essential hypertension. He denies fever or severe abdominal pain, but admits to reduced fluid intake. On examination: pulse 109 bpm, BP 141/95 mmHg, weight 65 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild generalized tenderness. Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis. Plan: a prescription was issued for the patient. He was advised to drink small sips of fluid often, eat rice, bananas, and toast, and wash his hands before eating. Follow-up in 2 days if the stools do not settle.
